Original painting or fine art print: which is right for you?

November 13, 2026 · From the Kimberly Marnell Art studio

You can love the same image in two different ways: as the original work made by the artist, or as a print that brings the image into your everyday space. The useful question is what you want to live with, at what scale and within what budget.

What you collect with an original

An original painting is the individual physical work. Its surface belongs to the material: a brush mark in oil, a translucent watercolor wash, or the edge of a drawn line. Photographs help you explore an artwork, but they cannot replace a close view of its texture. Ask for details or additional photographs if the surface matters to your decision.

Queen of the Night, for example, combines watercolor, acrylic marker and ink on paper. The original is offered unframed at $2,600. Flourish is an oil painting on canvas, offered at $1,500. These are different materials and individual works, rather than different print sizes of the same item.

What a fine art print offers

A print reproduces the image of an artwork. It gives you a way to choose a format and scale that suits your room without buying the unique original. The print listing should tell you the material, image size, framing options and who produces the order. A paper print and a canvas reproduction can present the same image differently.

Kimberly’s The Comfort of Frosting print page introduces paper and canvas options fulfilled by Saatchi Art. Follow the listing to confirm the current size, price, shipping and framing choices before ordering. A reproduction remains a print even when the source artwork was painted in oil.

Check the details before choosing

Measure the wall, then mark the artwork’s stated dimensions with paper or removable tape. Check whether those measurements describe the image, the paper or the outside of a frame. Look at the space in daylight and under your evening lighting. If framing is separate, leave room in your budget and measurements for it.

For a gift, a print lets the recipient choose a presentation that works in their home. An original can be a very personal choice; ask about the artwork before purchasing if you are unsure. Direct originals and marketplace prints have different purchase and return terms, so read the policy for the place where you pay.

Start with the image you keep returning to

You do not need to build a collection all at once. Begin with an artwork that holds your attention, then decide which form makes sense for you. If you love Kimberly’s subjects but need a particular size or palette, a personal painting commission is another route to discuss.
